releases.title: Preserve drafts during quick conversation switches
changes: Typing or sending in another conversation no longer cancels an unsaved draft from the previous conversation during its short save delay.
Draft saves stay attached to their original conversation, and sending does not restore stale draft text or send it to a different chat.

releases.title: Reliable restart recovery and saved conversations
changes: Invalid saved restart receipts no longer leave conversations and update actions blocked; the interrupted attempt remains recorded without claiming restart success.
Saved documents, diagrams, images and interactive surfaces reopen with their retained content after a host restart, while preserving conversation selection and unsent drafts.
Voice corrections are delivered to the existing conversation with their original request and approval boundaries intact.
Recovered background-work evidence is clearly labeled as a service update, while messages actually typed by the user retain their original attribution.
An older saved provider selection can resume through a uniquely matching configured instance of the same provider and model, preserving its saved reasoning effort.

releases.title: Reliable provider settings and connection checks
changes: Provider settings, model discovery and connection checks start correctly in the isolated runtime used by installed applications.
A provider helper that exits without a result now reports the exit status and recovery guidance instead of incorrectly saying dependencies are still installing.

releases.title: Preserve canvas resources across clients
changes: Storage cleanup retains canvas content, saved tool views, nested resources and attachments referenced by any client, including disconnected clients.
Startup and routine saves use complete shared and client state when checking which resource files remain in use.
A recovery action can restore missing content from exact hash-matching saved JSON while preserving artifact identities and without replaying tools.
The TUI host recommendation is now 0.11.9 or later; the documented live-client validation baseline remains 0.11.7.

notices.title: Update to protect saved canvas content
notices.detail: Earlier releases could delete resource files still referenced by saved canvas views during cleanup. This release prevents that deletion; it cannot reconstruct content already lost.
notices.action: Install this update. If a saved view reports unavailable content, recover it from an exact retained source or reopen the read-only view. Do not replay a tool action that changes data just to restore its display.

releases.title: Shared model settings for native runtimes
changes: An optional host adapter lets compatible native runtimes read shared provider settings from the user, workspace and native-session scopes while retaining their own domain bundles and instructions.
The adapter uses normal model routing, preserves delegated model preferences and keeps saved-session configuration checks. Installing this release does not enable it or change an existing manager.
A shareable TUI integration guide documents settings precedence, provider instances, credentials, routing, voice preferences and cross-app adoption checks.

releases.title: Reliable live-session activation and terminal client handoff
changes: A new live turn keeps session ownership while it is being scheduled, preventing a concurrent UI control from parking it before execution starts.
The runtime uses the reviewed loop-live scheduling correction across both session preparation and installed runtime dependencies.
The TUI developer handoff documents the supported connection, command, snapshot, retry and lifecycle contracts with validation boundaries.

releases.title: Clearer ecosystem update status
changes: Updates distinguish sources found in shared Amplifier settings from cached sources whose use is unknown, while keeping failures visible and eligible updates available.
Retained conversation history for missing workspace folders no longer causes a source-configuration warning.
Verified wiki-weaver build-generated version stamps no longer block ecosystem updates; genuine edits and unrecognized generated changes remain protected.

releases.title: Updates resume after inspecting runtime settings
changes: Opening a running mount plan or inspecting runtime settings no longer leaves application updates waiting indefinitely when the conversation is idle.
Updates continue to wait for accepted messages, starting workers, active calls, and unfinished runtime controls.
A runtime control that times out or loses its caller remains protected until the worker finishes or exits.

releases.title: Reliable drafts before the first conversation
changes: Typing before the first conversation now saves your draft without a validation error or creating a chat.
The unsent draft survives reload and stays private to that browser. Creating the first conversation carries the draft forward.
Delayed draft saves remain attached to their original composer and cannot overwrite a newly selected conversation.

releases.title: Release history and important update notices
changes: Updates now includes a changelog, with installed release notes available offline and upcoming notes loaded from the exact published release.
High-impact changes show what changed and what to do. Review status is shared across devices; reviewing clears the badge and keeps the notice in the changelog.
Release publishing now requires an authored changelog entry and uses it for GitHub release notes. This history begins with version 0.11.0.

releases.title: Reliable first launch and review acknowledgments
changes: An empty installation now opens with an editable composer; the first message creates one conversation.
Marking an Activity item reviewed stays responsive while a message send is waiting. Reviewing an older item cannot dismiss a newer occurrence.
Release checks now cover empty first launch and reviewing notices during a pending send.

releases.title: Live conversations across windows and devices
changes: Connected web windows and devices share accepted messages, live replies, approvals and running work.
Each browser keeps its own selected conversation, drafts, panels and canvas controls. Reload restores that browser's view; disconnecting leaves work running.
The service API and Python adapter support future terminal clients. A separate TUI application is not included in this release.
Shared configuration introduced in 0.11.0 is preserved.

notices.title: Devices share work and keep separate views
notices.detail: Messages and approvals affect the same live conversation across connected devices. Selecting another conversation or editing an unsent draft now affects only that browser. The first browser to attach inherits saved drafts from the previous shared view.
notices.action: Use the same conversation on another device to follow ongoing work. Check the first attached browser for drafts saved before this upgrade. Closing a browser does not stop the work.

releases.title: Shared Amplifier configuration
changes: Amplifier Unified reads the same ~/.amplifier/settings.yaml as Amplifier CLI, including providers, model routing, bundle defaults and voice preferences.
Workspace .amplifier/settings.yaml and settings.local.yaml override global defaults; existing session overrides remain in effect.
Provider credentials use the shared ~/.amplifier/keys.env and routing profiles use shared Amplifier locations.

notices.title: Settings now apply across Amplifier apps
notices.detail: Shared ~/.amplifier configuration is now authoritative. Changes to shared providers, routing and voice preferences can affect CLI and Unified sessions. Migration preserves existing shared values and keeps a backup of the previous private Unified settings; conflicting private values are not copied over shared values.
notices.action: Review providers, model routing and voice preferences after upgrading. Put project-specific choices in the workspace's .amplifier settings. If an old Unified choice is missing, compare the migration backup under ~/.amplifier-unified/backups/shared-settings-* before changing shared values.
